newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Senate passes $616 mln GO bond bill.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Senate passes $616 mln GO bond bill.

text.p: The Illinois Senate passed a $616 million general obligation bond authorization bill on Thursday, while Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar and legislative leaders met to try to resolve a standoff on House support for the measure.

The bill's passage by the Republican-controlled Senate sends the measure to the Democrat-controlled House where similar bonding bills have failed over the past two years to garner a required three-fifths majority vote.

No resolution was reached at the bond bill summit called by Edgar, a Republican, on Wednesday as a way to press for legislation to allow the state to issue bonds for prisons and other capital projects.
The governor called the legislature's failure to pass a bond authorization bill over the past two years "irresponsible" and "wrong."
Steve Brown, a spokesman for House Speaker Michael Madigan, D-Chicago, said the leaders agreed to have their staffs meet Friday, while the leaders and governor could meet again next week.

Brown said Madigan had not yet made any judgements on the bond bill. Madigan and House Democrats have declined in the past to increase the state's bond authorization, citing concerns about credit ratings and the amount of debt outstanding.
Last fall, Madigan said his members would support a pared down version of the bill that would allow about $200 million of GO bonds to be sold for prison construction.

Patty Schuh, a spokeswoman for Senate President James "Pate" Philip, R-Wood Dale, said the bill passed by the Senate also allows for $500 million of the $616 million of GO bonds to be sold as college savings bonds.
